To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the differential decondensation (DDC) of chromosomes is a cause of differential staining of chromosomes.

the chromosomal ultrastructure in Chinese hamster cells subjected to the action of a hypotonic solution is characterized by the uneven distribution of DNP fibrils along the chromatid, and the densely packed regions of the chromosomes correspond to G-banded regions.

hypotonic treatment results in differential decondensa-tion of chromosomes which consists of uneven distribution of DNP fibrils along chromatid, and that fixation with methanol acetoic acid causes a restructuration of chromosomes, but the uneven distribution of DNB along chromatids is preserved.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ultrastructural changes in chromosomes during the preparation of G-banding.
the ultrastructural mechanism of differential staining of chromosomes in hypotonic solutions.
the mechanism of G-banding and its relationship to the structure of mitotic chromosomes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
G-banding is caused by differential decondensation during hypotonic pretreatment.
the G-banding pattern is not a result of differential staining of chromosomes but rather of their differential decondensation during hypotonic treatments.
the G- and R- bands are differentially sensitive to the hypotonic treatment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
G-bands are not a result of differential staining but rather of differential decondensation.
differential decondensation is the most probable cause of G-bands in chromosomes.
the differential staining of chromosomes is a result of differential decondensation, i.e. the differential decondensation is the basis for the differential staining.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the differential staining of chromosomes in G-banding may be caused not only by differential condensation but also by differential decondensation.
G-banding is a consequence of differential decondensation, rather than differential staining of chromosomes.
differential staining of chromosomes is not a consequence of differential fixation of chromosomes but is a result of the differential decondensation induced by hypotonic treatment.
